correctness.rationale: For regular kappa, the transitive closures of B and A union {B} are unions of fewer than kappa sets each of hereditary size below kappa, so the witness z=A union {B} lies in H(kappa). Foundation excludes b in z and z in b for b in B, and also makes z fresh. Transfinite recursion of length at most kappa gives induced embeddings because every stage has fewer than kappa predecessors. In a rank-compatible well-order the earlier neighbors of x are exactly the members of x, so Col is at most kappa; the von Neumann ordinals below kappa form a clique of size kappa. The standard inequalities force clique, ordinary chromatic, list chromatic and coloring number all to equal kappa. K_{kappa^+} therefore cannot embed, giving the claimed sharp full-universality cutoff.
risks: The host H(kappa) can have cardinality above kappa; the claim concerns sizes of universally embedded target graphs, not host cardinality.
No singular-kappa extension claim is established.
